## What is Quarto?

+ Interactive reports
+ Markdown based
+ Computation inside the file!

````{.md filename="report_file.qmd" code-line-numbers=""}

format: html
Author: "Andrey Höglund"
date: Today
---

The main results of the analysis were ...

```{.r}

```
````

## What is Quarto?

- An open-source scientific and technical publishing system
- Built on Pandoc — write in Markdown, output anywhere
- The **next generation** of R Markdown (but not R-only)
- Created by Posit (formerly RStudio)

::: {.notes}
Quarto lets you turn plain text into polished documents, presentations, websites, and books.
:::

---

## Why Quarto?

| Feature | Benefit |
|---|---|
| Multi-language | R, Python, Julia, Observable JS |
| Multi-format | HTML, PDF, Word, Revealjs, and more |
| Single source | One `.qmd` file → many outputs |
| Reproducible | Code + prose live together |

---

## Installing Quarto

1. Download from [quarto.org](https://quarto.org)
2. Install the CLI (works on macOS, Linux, Windows)
3. Use with your favourite editor:
   - VS Code (official extension)
   - RStudio (built-in)
   - Jupyter
   - Neovim

---

## Anatomy of a `.qmd` File

```{.yaml filename="example.qmd"}
---
title: "My Document"
format: html
---

## A heading

Some text and a code chunk:

```

A `.qmd` file = **YAML front matter** + **Markdown** + **code chunks**

---

## Code Chunks in Action

````markdown
```r
library(tidyverse)
df <- read_csv("data.csv")
summary(df)
```
````

- Code runs at render time
- Output (tables, plots) is embedded automatically
- Use `echo: false` to hide code, `eval: false` to skip execution

---

## Output Formats

Change one line in the YAML to switch formats:

```yaml
format: html        # interactive web page
format: pdf         # LaTeX-quality PDF
format: docx        # Word document
format: revealjs    # slide deck (like this one!)
format: dashboard   # interactive dashboard
```

One source, many destinations.

---

## Rendering

From the terminal:

```bash
quarto render my-file.qmd
```

Or preview with live reload:

```bash
quarto preview my-file.qmd
```

VS Code & RStudio also offer one-click render buttons.

---

## Beyond Single Documents

Quarto can power entire **projects**:

- **Websites** — blogs, documentation sites
- **Books** — multi-chapter with cross-references
- **Dashboards** — interactive data apps
- **Manuscripts** — journal-ready articles with citations

All configured through a `_quarto.yml` project file.

---

## Tips & Tricks

- Use `#| label: fig-plot` to cross-reference figures
- Add `freeze: true` to cache expensive computations
- Publish instantly with `quarto publish` (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Quarto Pub)
- Parameterised reports: pass variables at render time

---

## Get Started Now

1. Install → `quarto.org`
2. Create → `quarto create project`
3. Write → mix Markdown and code
4. Render → `quarto render`
5. Publish → `quarto publish`

**Your 300 seconds are up — go build something!** 🚀

Full docs: [quarto.org/docs](https://quarto.org/docs)
